The tremendous upsurge in use of hallucinogenic and other drugs in the past decade has led to the enactment of new State and Federal laws prohibiting their manufacture, sale, possession, and use. Probably the most popular and widely used of these substances, especially among young people, is marijuana. In Pulaski County, Indiana, there are 65 square acres of wild growing marijuana. It is estimated that unless removed thousands of pounds of wild marijuana will be picked by young people coming into the State for this specific purpose. Much publicity has been generated by the underground press regarding the Pulaski marijuana fields.
The Prosecutor's Office, Winamac, Indiana has requested a $3,000 grant to destroy the marijuana fields in Pulaski County and to prevent the reestablishment of the plant in future years. The Prosecutor's Office claims that less than 10 percent of the pickers can be stopped and that thousands of pounds of marijuana will be picked and transported throughout the country if the marijuana plants are not sprayed. Since wild hemp is an annual, reproducing only by seed, it is important to prevent seed production. Herbicides provide simple, low cost control. Chemical 2, 4D sprayed on the plants when they are young, growing and not more than 24 inches high, will prevent regrowth.
The grant will be used to spray the area involved over a one day period by helicopter. Spraying will be at the 20 percent level. The subcontractor, Clarke Outdoor Spraying Company of La Grange, Illinois, states that spraying can be accomplished within an accuracy of two feet
